text:
Lee: Heads-up — since ~03:10 UTC we're seeing recurring tail-latency spikes on eu2 dedicated pool. Telemetry narrows to NVLink transmit saturation on 4 nodes (rack42). This looks like cross-tenant transfer bursts (large-model KV cache fills) causing stalls and long tail lat.

Ben: Can you paste the node telemetry lines?

Lee: logs:
```
node=eu2-rack42-gpu05 nvlink_tx=98% 2025-11-17T03:12Z
gpu0: stall_ms=72 kvcache_fill=1.2GB
dmesg: nvlink timeout ack
```

Sasha: Hmm. Is this confined to shared warm pool or are tenants pinned to dedicated slices?

Lee: It's mixed — a few tenants are on dedicated-slice but others on shared-warm on same host via vGPU. NVLink TX across the board is saturated when big offloads happen.

Maria: Two quick levers: 1) route high-IO tenants to the dedicated-burst pool (pre-warmed A10 quanta), 2) add an NVLink bandwidth tag to routing policy so scheduler avoids mixing high-NV tenants with others.

Ben: What about cost and rollback plan?

Maria: Cost estimate rough: moving 5 tenants -> 4x A10 pre-warmed reserved for burst ~ $220/day delta. But tradeoff: reduce retry/durable fallback costs and SLO penalties which we've been hitting.

Sasha: Can we do a 30m canary reroute for 2 tenants (low risk) and monitor tail/egress metrics? If green, scale to 5.

Lee: Sounds good. @ops-oncall can you take the canary at 14:00 UTC? We'll set routing tag 'nvlink-avoid' on the canary.

ops-oncall: I'll run it. Creating a short runbook now.

infra-bot: Incident created INC-2025-4323 for tracking. Playbook: reroute -> watch nvlink_tx and tail_p50/p99 -> rollback after 30m if tail_p99>200ms.

Sasha: Runbook snippet for routing service:
```
routing.modify({
  match: "tenant.metadata.nv_intensive == true",
  prefer: "pool:dedicated-burst",
  fallback: "pool:shared-warm",
  canary: { percent: 10, duration_mins: 30 }
})
```

Ben: After canary, let's also consider a longer term change: mark tenants with heavy model KV cache ops and give them an nvlink_bandwidth_quota to drive autoscaling/pinning decisions.

Lee: Agreed. Action items: Sasha run canary @14:00 UTC; Maria to produce cost delta spreadsheet; Ben to draft quota proposal; ops-oncall to monitor and report. :thumbsup:
